Bingkun Qi · Academic Affairs System

How can a form tutor see a pupil’s week across subjects?

My colleagues used to piece together a pupil’s week from several Excel sheets. I built a shared database where subject teachers enter their observations and a form tutor can read all the reports for one pupil and see which are still due.

At school I saw colleagues switch between sheets less often. I have yet to measure the time saved or the effect on pupils’ learning.

Week 4 · Fictional pupil record

A physics comment and a missing maths report

When the form tutor opens the weekly record, physics has a grade and maths is still blank. Who should the tutor speak to, and about what?

One pupil, seen by two teachers

  1. The physics teacher records an observation — The pupil completed two of three homework tasks. The teacher records an overall C and adds a reminder to check how the pupil finds the intercept on a graph next lesson.
  2. The form tutor opens the same week — The physics grade and comment are visible in the pupil’s record. Alongside them, maths is marked “未填” (report pending).
  3. The tutor can follow up with two people — The tutor can ask the pupil to show how they read the intercept on their physics graph. For maths, the next step is to ask the teacher for the missing report.

Inside the Academic Affairs System

The first two modules support the weekly feedback case. I also built tools for timetable changes, rosters, assessment records and teaching hours. I have held back wider use of these tools at school because they involve more pupil data.

01

Weekly subject reports

Teachers can enter feedback by class, copy the previous week’s records and add an observation for each pupil.

02

The form tutor’s overview

Tutors can read comments across subjects for each pupil and identify the subjects whose reports are due.

03

Timetable changes

Teachers can request a move, an extra lesson or cover. Administrators review requests and update the existing timetable.

04

Class lists and teaching assignments

Administrators maintain class lists and teaching assignments. If a subject has no named teacher, they can check the pupil’s enrolment and the teaching assignment for that subject.

05

Exam and homework records

Teachers can set up an exam and enter marks, or open a homework task and record completion by class. Each has its own entry screen.

Screenshot gap: exam/homework pages still need local init_db --demo captures (never production). Copy-only for now.

06

Teaching hours and exports

The current timetable and extra lessons supply the hours report. Staff can export a CSV, and the system logs the export. Historical cover needs a separate check.

What I would check before wider use

I would ask a subject teacher and a form tutor to walk through one reporting week together before deciding whether to add another class.

Evaluation

Can staff find the missing report?

Ask colleagues to find the subject still due for one pupil using the spreadsheets and then the system. Record time taken, sheet changes and whether they identify the right subject.

Access

Who needs this record?

Agree with the school which pupils and fields each role should see before choosing the next class for a pilot.
